title: Service Bus vs. Event Grid vs. Event Hubs
description: Compare the three main Azure messaging services and learn when to choose each one.

data.text: Azure offers three distinct messaging services, each designed for a different purpose. Choosing the wrong service can lead to unnecessary complexity, higher costs, or reliability issues. Here is a simple guide to help you decide.

data.title: When to Use Each
items: Service Bus: Order processing, payment workflows, inventory updates -- anything requiring ordered, reliable delivery with retries.
Event Grid: Reacting to changes in Azure resources (blob uploads, VM state changes), serverless workflows with many subscribers.
Event Hubs: IoT telemetry, application metrics, log aggregation, clickstream data -- high-volume data streams.

cards.title: Service Bus
cards.description: Reliable enterprise messaging with FIFO, sessions, and transactions.

cards.title: Event Grid
cards.description: Fast event routing from Azure services to your handlers.

cards.title: Event Hubs
cards.description: Scalable streaming platform for high-volume telemetry.

data.title: Mix and Match
data.text: You can use all three services in the same application. Service Bus handles commands, Event Grid handles state-change events, and Event Hubs handles high-volume telemetry.

data.title: Choose the Right Azure Messaging Service
data.description: For each scenario, select the best Azure messaging service and explain why.
steps: Process payment transactions in strict order with retries.
Notify 5 different microservices when a new customer record is created.
Ingest 100,000 device heartbeats per second for a monitoring dashboard.
Route file-upload events to image-processing, virus-scanning, and indexing services.
data.expectedOutcome: 1: Service Bus, 2: Event Grid (topic), 3: Event Hubs, 4: Event Grid.
